《终末机兵》是一款以沙盒探索与回合制战斗为主的角色扮演游戏。游戏中玩家身处一个末世的世界，人类与机械的战斗中，人类落败了，世界被机械所统治，为了打破这个僵局，玩家将扮演雇佣兵小队驾驶机甲与这些邪恶的机械对抗，从他们的手中夺回整个世界。 [h1]自由探索的大地图[/h1] 游戏的地图非常庞大，并且任由玩家在其中自由探索。当然玩家的每次移动都会消耗燃油，玩家需要回到基地补充燃油，才能前往更远的地方。这提供了游戏的真实性，并且也让玩家在逐渐的扩大可移动的范围和探索的内容，让玩家明显感觉到有所成长。 [h1]热血漫画般电影式的画面表现[/h1] 游戏的画面应该是这款游戏最大的卖点，也是我最喜欢这款游戏的地方。无论是游戏的剧情过场部分还是战斗部分都采用了电影式的流畅动画展现，并且非常有热血漫画的味道，画面风格有点《Kill la kill》的即视感，热血而有趣。玩家的一部机甲需要有4名驾驶员，分别拥有不同的职责和技能。游戏的战斗玩法也非常有趣，采用了一种独特的时序系统。但是游戏的教程部分并没有介绍的很详细，一笔带过。让玩家初始的游玩有点懵逼，但是熟悉了游戏的玩法和节奏之后，体验就会有所提升。 [h1]时序系统的回合制战斗玩法[/h1] 游戏的战斗通常是通过剧情的发展和接取一些委托来进行的，玩家需要驾驶自己的飞船前往目的地进行战斗。战斗的展开采用回合制的基本系统加上时序系统的独特玩法。每个回合中，玩家需要为自己的4名驾驶员安排行动，并选择穿插在时序的什么位置。每个行动都有自己的优先度，一旦行动时序与敌人重合了，就会根据优先度判断敌我双方谁先行动。优先度高的会优先行动。如果敌我双方的优先度相同，则会默认玩家先行动。玩家就需要在时序系统中，安排队员们的行动顺序，以最大化行动效率。 [h1]游戏同样包含一些养成玩法[/h1] 虽然游戏的队员玩家无法自由自定义，只能通过随机生成的方式生成4名队员。但是在游戏的过程中，这些队员始终伴随着玩家进行，时间久了也自然会产生一些感情。游戏中玩家也需要对这些队员进行士气的管理和机甲的养成等部分，提升战斗的能力，从而不断推进剧情向前发展。 [table][td][b]欢迎关注我们 [/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10591434/]突突突发糖辣！[/url] [/td][/table]

评价是典型的游戏性给画风建模磕一个的游戏，我虽然给了好评但是现阶段内容还是有点少，不太能撑得起反复游玩。 虽然说画风很好，但是游戏好像锁六十帧，而且不能调整分辨率。可能由于战斗动画的实时演算导致实际上主打的战斗画面可能只有个位数的帧数。再由于队员只能随机生成，导致不roll初始就要跟四个妖魔鬼怪一同游戏了。大地图和各个城镇都做的很漂亮，怪物做的也挺有特色。 游戏性方面整体难度不高，打不动怪了就多去刷刷委托，玩起来比较像之前玩过的符文竞技场，但是又没有那么复杂。基本上就是见招拆招，司机和炮手尽量后动，让敌人先把意图都先露出来再决定是打输出还是换位躲避伤害。 然后要提到的一点就是大地图，感觉可有可无，先阶段又大又空，🤔刷委托还需要几个城市来回跑，导致几乎跑图时间和战斗时间都是对半开，还有明明是飞艇却越不过山，导致强行拖时间绕圈。并且虽然开局主线给了个声纳说可以探测和打捞大地图的物资，但是对此的指引完全只有对声纳的描述那一句话，具体怎么操作或者说怎么触发只字不提。感觉把大地图删了改成那种小号的地图都不影响游戏体验。而且说实话这种游戏类型更适合rouge lite，但是既然已经订好了游戏内容我觉得也挺不错的。 希望正式版能做的更好吧

有着以赛璐璐为主的美术风格兼极具张力的、模仿日本机器人动画中常见分镜风格的演出效果，《终末机兵》是一款结合了部分养成元素的、以机器人为主要题材的回合制战术角色扮演游戏。独特的游戏机制和部分形似扳机社又具有欧美风格的人设/画面，是它主要突出的部分所在。 [h2]特色与优点[/h2] 《终末机兵》的主打战斗设计，在于将传统回合制游戏中受角色属性值（如速度、敏捷等）影响的轮次更替转变为以我方/敌方在时间轴上的先后次序、玩家对角色的行动安排和我方机体的站位等多重因素来共同决定的轮次行动，从而大大地拓展了游戏在战术层面上的选择和组合。 在同一时间轴轮次上，敌我的行动次序取决于所选择行动的数字大小，同时又可能受到我方or敌方站位或是采取的部分行动的影响，从而被取消或是行动无效化；而我方的人物也有可能因敌方的战斗效果受伤或是受到负面效果影响（如情绪低落），从而或是使得角色暂时失去作战能力，或是间接令角色可能产生某些不可控制的负面行为，甚至直接以死亡的方式失去该角色。游戏难度越高，由上述效果所产生的负面影响则越为明显。故而玩家想要规划好每一场战斗，试图造成最低的损失和最大的胜利，那么其中的要点即在于尽可能地通过某些行动或是从敌人的行为模式上汲取经验来做出应对敌人的准确判断，并以自身的行动尽可能地打断或是取消敌人的行动所造成的影响。 为了达到上述这一目的，除了利用不同的人物之间具有的特性、机体各部分可选择的行动效果和与敌机的相对站位外，对机体部件的换装是最能直接影响我方机体整体强度和战术组合的高效选择。譬如，当玩家更换上具有高数值近战杀伤效果的肩部部件和可更换站位的手臂部件，而敌人的类型多为缺乏移动的远程战斗机体时，选择利用手臂部件提供的区域位移进行贴近敌人的移动，用近战攻击（玩家甚至可以利用胸部部件来为近战效果提供伤害加成）来对敌人造成高额伤害，并在这之后利用核心部件提供的释放烟雾来闪避敌人的远程攻击，就可以作为效率最高的战术组合选择。相反地，玩家亦可以利用出色的远程武器和频繁的位移调整来应对具有多段伤害的部分擅长近战的敌人，以防止这类敌人的近战攻击对玩家的机体造成大量伤害。 另一重影响到玩家所采取的战术组合的主要因素，即为具体角色战术选择界面中的“势能转移”（类似女神异闻录系列战斗中的换手选项），而想要执行这一选项，则需要特定的人际关系（竞争or密友）作为支持，故而队伍内角色之间的情感关系培养亦是在关键时刻决定胜利天秤倾斜的重要部分。玩家想要对不同的角色之间进行关系栽培，除了经历部分涉及此类效果的、可被触发的随机事件外，必须利用中间人提供的自由任务中获得的（或是战斗获胜后给予的）“代币”来在飞艇内部进行某些需要双人参与的、能提高/降低被选择角色的人物关系的相应活动，才能逐步在各个角色之间建立起密友/劲敌的关系，从而在战斗中部分角色所提供的行动效果性价比不高时，利用“势能转移”所提供的额外行动点数来实现同一个角色的多次行动，以此实现诸如快速击杀棘手敌人这样的行动效果。 除了战术搭配和选择上的多样性外，富有张力和场面感的动画演出同样也是本作作为机器人题材游戏的一大卖点。玩家在战斗中安排好时间轴上的各项行动后，点击对相应的行动组和进行执行，即可观看由这些行动和敌方的行动反馈所共同组成的战斗演出。像是机身内的角色夸张地操纵按钮和摇杆，或是敌机在玩家的近战/远程攻击下倒地毁灭这样的情景组合，加上经由玩家的精确战术安排所产生的正反馈效果，足以调动玩家对于编排属于自己的战斗动画的参与感。 [h2]尚显不足之处[/h2] 由于本作目前刚刚发售不久，且处于抢先体验阶段，仅仅实装了基础的游戏框架和与之相应的大致体验，尚有着许多亟待开发和增添的内容，故而游戏在进行到一定程度后所带来的将是高重复度的单一体验。除此之外，游戏中也包含了部分设计上可能存在着的问题。主要的一些让人产生欠佳体验的部分如下： [b]1、UI信息呈现时的杂乱无章：[/b] 不难看出，本作的部分UI设计（如飞艇内界面的UI）所试图模仿的对象是《女神异闻录5》，像是飞艇内二层的休息室和娱乐室内的一些UI（如将棋、吉他等），就明显具有与之相似的风格特征。然而，在飞艇内部的主要界面内，除了形象明晰的我方机甲机身外，在其他区域的色块交叠下，两个可交互的UI置身其中并不具备高辨识度，且UI提供的功能信息极其模糊（“一层”和“健身房”能告知玩家的直接信息是什么？），只有在鼠标靠近UI后才会显示具体文字内容。点击“一层”UI后，飞艇内部其他各层的UI显示莫不如是，更有甚者在某些场景下左下角的部分UI会同背景相应的区域色块混淆在一起，无法形成明确的区别。此外，虽然如“打开菜单”这样的页面UI显示在设计上有所集中，但飞艇内部的UI功能分布过于散漫和随意，需要玩家通过一层层点击来进行跳转，极其不便且互相之间缺乏逻辑关联。反观P5，不但在UI设计和与UI配套的界面设计上通过合理的配色做出了明确的区分，而且相关UI所传递的功能信息十分清晰，且UI之间也通过合适的排布逻辑集中在一定的区域内。这些部分的设计要点，都是制作组在今后的更新中所亟需考虑到的。 [b]2、基础功能的简陋和缺失：[/b] 当玩家用PC来进行游戏时，在不使用手柄的前提下，游戏中绝大部分的操作只能通过鼠标来进行完成，缺乏对一些相关功能的自定义快捷键设置。玩家的飞艇只能通过鼠标或者键盘十字键来进行航行操作，无法进行诸如设置路径自动航行等操作，在中期需要玩家在地图上进行长时间跑任务的情况下略显费劲。最为要命的是，游戏中虽然有着小地图窗口显示这一设计，却缺乏最基本的整体地图显示，导致玩家在游戏中经常会出现天地虽大，却浑然不觉自己该去向何处的尴尬情况。 [b]3、大而空旷且存在要素显示缺失的地图：[/b] 说到地图，就不得不提同样令人糟心的地图设计。除了目前体验阶段的大地图极为空旷，且可触发事件数量少/种类较为单一外，地图中存在着的障碍物（如绵延的山脉）与其他的地图区块之间并不存在明显的区分设计，只有当玩家一头撞上后方才能知道相应部分是无法通行的区域。此外，整体地图显示的缺失也使得玩家无法手动标注目标地点来在小地图上进行导航，再加上大地图中存在着多个有着不同任务、设施和物品的独立城市，玩家必须在这些城市之间往返来完成区域任务或是中间人提供的任务，故而玩家只能通过个人记忆来识别这些城市所处的大致方位，否则在未接到相应任务前，便只能在空阔的地图中漫无目的地探索，直到偶然遇见这些城市中的一部分。 [b]4、略呈繁杂的战术界面操作步骤：[/b] 战斗中，玩家并不能直接选择具体驾驶员进行行动，因为不同的功能选择被区分成了具有层级显示的嵌套界面，只有在点进驾驶员列表并且随后点击具体驾驶员后，各驾驶员的可执行动作才会被清晰地显示出来。此外，由于执行交战行动时敌人一次只能呈现一个，且不同的敌人在时间轴之间的识别度区分并不明显（选择时，只有淡淡的一层闪烁边框提示），故而可能会导致玩家产生诸如因误触而错选攻击对象的情况。建议制作组调整这两个方面的设计。 [b]5、粗糙的养成系统和成长缓慢的升级系统：[/b] 游戏中玩家队伍中所携带的各类角色的各项能力，只能通过在战斗中担任具体位置，于战斗胜利后得到成长（一次只能提升对应的一项），或是通过阅读相关的能力培训书籍来进行增进，而目前游戏所能提供的成长途径除随机事件外就只有这两种选择。随着角色的等级逐步提升，虽然会获得额外的角色能力，但各项能力的属性值成长也会变得逐渐缓慢起来，像是角色作为见习级别时提供的经验成长就已经寥寥无几，提升到下一等级所需经历的战斗数量只会随此愈来愈多，反而不如玩家在愚人旅店直接雇佣高等级驾驶员来得明快。此外，部分游戏中有物品出售的养成内容（如植物、料理等）并未实装（也可能是笔者并未游玩到大后期的缘故？），亟待这些内容能确实地得到使用和体验的那一天。 以上所陈述的内容，便是《终末机兵》目前所能为玩家带来的主要体验。尽管有着一些影响这种体验的瑕疵和缺陷存在，但只要制作组能充分打磨并慎重考虑后续内容的更新和未来游戏的完善方向，本作还是有着相当程度的成长空间的。

I had high hopes, but the game just doesn't bring much to the table. For starters, no matter how much you can customize it, having only one mech to deploy will severely limit your options. The crew takes forever to level up, to the point where I wouldn't be able to get them even 1 level before I fell out of my refund window, and since combat actions are based around what parts the mech has equipped I assume the levels aren't very helpful anyway. Early battles are a slog, since you are always outnumbered and have limited means to attack. I suspect this doesn't improve either because, again, you only have one mech so you will just give it the best load out and every fight will be the same.

[h1]最灼热的不是机炮火光，而是撞向绝望时眼底残存的微光[/h1] [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44900613]“黄油收集师”[/url][/td][/table] [h1]一、机甲交响曲与废土生存诗[/h1] 《终末机兵》是由DESTINYbit打造的一款以时序轴策略为核心的机甲题材战术RPG。游戏中玩家将化身雇佣兵指挥官，在机械统治的末世中驾驶飞艇穿梭于十几座人类据点，通过合约任务维系小队生存，同时培育驾驶员间的战友情谊与个人成长。游戏流程预计20小时（本人安稳发育派的所以前期流程较长），以沙盒式开放世界为舞台，不过没有规避掉地图空洞的毛病，但是每一次燃油消耗的航行决策以及机甲改装资源与驾驶员心理状态，形成了“生存压力”与“少年热血漫”的奇异组合。本作将战术深度倾注于动态的时序安排。战斗UI被具象化为四人的机甲操控舱：下屏实时显示敌我行动轴，左侧分列驾驶员状态面板。这种设计不仅将“回合制”转化为动画分镜脚本创作，更通过驾驶员崩溃时的指令失控、英雄时刻的自主行动表现，让“机甲人格化”的主题穿透玩法与叙事的壁垒。 [h1]二、时序齿轮与人文生态[/h1] [h3]1、时序战斗：动画分镜师般的策略编排[/h3] 游戏独创的四职协同系统要求玩家同时扮演战术家与动画导演：机体驾驶员闪避移动与危险防御操作、枪炮手蓄力射击的时机与驾驶员的呐喊、工程师冷却过载引擎的手忙脚乱，均在一条动态时间轴上并行推进。当规划阶段结束，所有指令将以三渲二动画演出呈现——导弹通过机甲臂暴力弹出、双手格挡的慢镜震颤，皆赋予玩家的决策以肉眼可见的电影级张力。 [h3]2、人文生态：机甲战斗背后的人性[/h3] 飞艇不仅是移动基地，更是驱动游戏情感的微缩社会。通过活动点数分配，玩家需安排驾驶员放松、训练、阅读等，甚至通过“特殊事件”触发角色羁绊事件。 遗憾的是，机甲改装与人物养成的权重失衡略显遗憾。数十种武器模块与散热系统的组合虽具深度，但驾驶员随机生成的背景故事缺乏事件支撑，使“伙伴/家庭”主题稍显流于表面。 反而危机时刻的设计更凸显人性维度：士气低迷时驾驶员可能违抗指令甚至畏缩在最后才行动，濒死状态触发“超越极限”的日漫式爆种。这种机制与叙事的咬合，使每场战斗都成为角色成长的隐喻，机甲伤痕是驾驶员心理创伤的实体映射。搭配上优秀的动画演出，让飞艇中缺乏塑造的人物形象一下子在战斗中变得立体起来了。 [h1]三、省流总结[/h1] 游戏标签：时序制战术RPG、机甲改装、废土生存。核心体验：动画级战斗演出、社群管理、开放世界（?）。

[h1]《终末机兵》：有一定特色的动漫风机甲作品，但实际游玩下来体验不佳[/h1] 在这也不扯什么游戏题材机甲的起源特征之类的注水科普了，一言概括笔者对尚处EA状态的《终末机兵》的游玩感受就是：高重复的可玩内容加上让人难绷的系统优化实在是对不起游戏商店页面下宣传的动漫美术和战斗系统~诚然机械末世四人小队共同操控机甲的各个部分抵御机械造物的排轴回合制玩法在同题材作品中实属少见，采用的类莫比斯美术风格和战斗中各行动的动画也算独树一帜，而游戏地图的空洞感以及无聊的主线任务角色养成亦是可见一斑：接任务-跑图-打怪三点一线循环往复~俯视角大地图上除了哨站还是哨站、接取的任务内容除了打架还是打架、养成的触发事件除了跑图还是跑图、更不要说角色战斗还有死亡这一设计让你小心翼翼时时注意保存……所以吐槽了这么多，咱玩这游戏到底图个啥呢？对于机甲作正常来说也就是希望自己配备零件提升性能然后能在战场上虐爆对面……吗？呃，其实游戏也不是这样~它唯一让人觉得有意思的地方就是战斗中通过排列行动指令以触发系列动画的新奇演出，只可惜一指令对应一个动画来来回回那么几套看几遍就腻了，加之优化不好掉帧卡顿时有发生，想玩的朋友建议还是过了EA再说吧 [h1]回合战斗机甲装配[/h1] 人类与机械爆发大战，结果输的一败涂地，世界已被机械占领。玩家作为雇佣兵小队的指挥官，依靠承接城市的合约任务谋生，说白了就是要和机械怪物们战斗。《终末机兵》的战斗设计于我而言还挺新奇——大体上来说是回合制，但更考较玩家对敌人行动的预测和其解决方法。具体一点的玩法是：每回合在分为六个单位的行动轴上，敌我双方都能各自在这条轴上放置行动指令，不同的行动指令可能有需要不同的连续的单位数。比如我给这条行动轴上的单位标号为1、2、3、4、5、6，敌人可能在3、4单位布置了攻击指令，所以我就可以选择消耗三个单位在234或者345上布置防御指令以免疫普通射击和减少炮弹伤害。机甲的四个驾驶员每回合各有一次布置行动指令的机会，结束后就可以观看动画静待博弈结果啦~值得一提的是回合中敌人也有着自己的指令次数，部分指令只会在玩家行动后布置，这种不确定性加上游戏不俗的难度也在一定程度上也使笔者不少次阴沟翻船 其他方面：除了回合内这种交叉式的依靠指令时序关系的战斗玩法令人惊喜，终末机兵还有着位置这一概念——战场分为东南西北四个区域。如果敌我不同处于一片区域就只能使用炮弹等远程攻击，反之则可以近身肉搏（伤害不俗）不过这个时候使用炮弹双方都会受到伤害。另外如果敌我在同一行动单位分别使用炮弹和突进，突进的优先级是高于发射炮弹的——这意味着此时敌我会同时受到伤害~当然游戏的区域分化也不仅仅只是限制近战，之后也有类似布置陷阱之类的技能。所以就战斗设计方面，本作还是很有意思的 [h1]角色养成属性提升[/h1] 除了机甲的各项装备，本作主要的提升方向就是关于人物的角色养成~在游戏的开始玩家可以去随机ROLL选四个初始属性较低的角色来当我们的机甲驾驶员，因此初始战斗部分各个驾驶员的技能极少~开始操作员就是释放烟雾；工程师能为机甲添加冷却剂防止因为行动会累计热量熄火BUSHI也能装填弹药；司机可以操作移动并能近战攻击；枪炮手则能进行远程伤害。当后来随着任务的推进经历战斗触发事件，角色们的射击电子工程等属性也会逐步提高会拥有更多的技能：地雷、治疗、过载、追踪……角色间也有关系条，达到一定程度即可在战斗中将自己的行动次数转让给队友，类似于女神异闻录的拍手~成功完成任务还可能获得特殊代币，用于提升关系条和情绪。同时角色在战斗部分还有士气值的设定：恐惧低落不能行动、情绪高涨几率暴击……而如果机甲严重受击的话驾驶员可能会直接晕厥，战斗结束后没挺过来就会死亡！没错，就是人没了的意思，接下来要不就读档，要不就去哨站花钱招人~说实话我觉得这个设计还是有怪恶心的，少见的养成游戏死角色 [h1]各方面吐槽和建议[/h1] 应个首尾呼应结尾就在这继续吐槽了：首先是机甲游戏爱好者的自定义模块实在太过简陋~基本上就是稍微变个形状然后换个颜色，不像《百万吨级武藏》或者《装甲核心：境界天火》那样更换部件有较大变化的同时还有条纹贴纸之类的涂装部分；本作开始还有ROLL角色的环节，但每次还会给你塞几个非主流~实际它就是固定的几个发型动作之类随机组的，并且时而角色还有高度重合。那既然这样我觉得还不如让玩家自己捏人~不过自定义这玩意不完善也没事，主要是就是游戏隶属机甲的浪漫没有体现，开机甲就是要帅要展现力量好吧~而游戏剧情里根本就没有对照组，无法以小人物来突出机甲驾驶者的责任和强大：在剧情上那真是向导的一条龙服务，都没怎么出现其他角色；而在战斗方面，每次都是相同的动画并且场景还都是平原，没有倒下压碎建筑物，也没有因为各种武器的使用导致环境崩坏——如此机甲的侵略感和破环感又从何而来呢？同样出现这问题的还有战斗的难度梯度：我努力赚钱更换机甲装备狂接任务养成角色不就是为了虐爆敌人吗？结果这破游戏我一成长怪物也成长了，那不相当于没成长嘛QAQ这导致游戏战斗从始至终都是煎熬的，想问制作组到底有没有玩过自己的游戏呀喂！ I wanted to like this game, but currently, it feels like a game with one cool gimmick that will get really old really fast. +/- I love the combat animations, but not the combat system itself. While I love how the animations feel like you're in an anime, there isn't any animation variety, and so you'll eventually see the animations play over and over ad nauseum. I hope the developer adds more animations to the same moves you do so it doesn't get stale. The combat system itself I don't want to bash because I think it's just not for me personally, but it might be for others. I will say however, that currently, I don't know if there's a way to fix a pilot when they go into a breakdown, but when that happens it's basically the same as losing the fight so I just reload the save. Not very fun tbh. +/- I like the downtime gameplay, of doing things to bond with your party members, but it's ruined by these "activity tokens". You need currency in order to just chill in your home base with your crew? doesn't make sense to me at all in gameplay and lore perspective. Stuff like this makes more sense when your currency is time like in other games. If this game had a system like Persona where your actions caused time to move and so you could only do a limited amount of activities a day, I'd be more forgiving, but instead you're using coins? huh? This system needs an over-haul and fast. - You can get softlocked by the game and it's not good at all. I played the tutorial, still in the tutorial I think, when I got my first "fixer" job to fight a mech. This mech demolished me and my crew and they all got "worried" and my mech got trashed. After the fight, I couldn't replay the fight because my crew and mech aren't ready (says an error message), and so I fix my mech up with scrap I had, but I still have the message and can't do the fight at all. I'm thinking maybe it's because my team's morale dropped and they were "worried", but I can't even tell you if that's the case because I don't have activity tokens to test if improving their morale would help, or if activities can change their worried status. This is why I dislike the activity system and how terribly it's implemented and I feel like it needs an over-haul. Maybe some other parts of the game need an over-haul too because being forced to load an older save or start all over is not fun at all and I can see people quitting the game because of it. EDIT: from the devs themselves, it seems that the issue I had was because my teammates were also injured, and apparently there's a city nearby with healing capabilities that the game doesn't even make you aware of yet. So I wanted to add this to the review for context. - The world is so empty and boring. I don't understand why we need to fly around the dead empty map when there's nothing enjoyable about it. You also waste fuel doing so and so you have to waste currency on refilling your fuel each time you go do anything. I'm assuming the dev intends on filling the world up to make this mean something? I sure hope so because at the moment, it's just something annoying that makes an already tedious game more tedious. + I really fell in love with the character creation of this game. TBH it's the reason I bought the game in the first place since I thought having random pilots was lame and I wouldn't feel attached to them to care about doing activities to improve their morale and friendship. I hope the dev keeps improving on the character creation with more options for characters. I hope they either allow males/females to use all hairstyles, or at least add more long hair options for males since guys have long hair too. These are my overall impressions with what little I've played of the game, but because it's early access, I want the devs to take this feedback and improve the game and make it better. I'd be more than happy to change my review whenever that happens, but for now, buyer beware!

Outside of battles your crew can randomly interact with each other, or you can send them to do various leisure activities all accompanied with numerous animations. Controls are excellent both with a controller or mouse and keyboard. It really shows that the game was made by fans of action mecha anime, and if you are too, you are going to love what they created here, you will really get the whole "look ma I'm in an action anime!" feeling. The animations accompanying all your actions is just pure awesomness. You will feel incontrol, and when you see your group of 4 working together to succeed just beats everything. I'm not gonna talk about the art style and overall graphics much, because, one: you can just look at the screenshots and decide if you like it or not, and two: to me that never mattered much, it can feel cheap, but it goes perfectly well with the old school neo japanese anime style its going for. The game has a very interesting art style, but almost everything else falls short for me. The turnbased gameplay feels shallow and poorly balanced, mostly because of the way each member of your 4 person party controls a different aspect of the mech. On paper, it sounds like an interesting concept but in practice the Gunner and Driver feel infinitely more useful than the Operator and Engineer. A lot of encounters end up feeling like I’m skipping their turns or baton passing because certain roles just don’t contribute nearly as much. At least in the Monki mech, even after getting multiple legendary upgrades. Maybe the balance improves later with the other mechs, but based on what I’ve heard from EA players, that apparently isn’t the case. The combat balance especially falls apart once multiple enemies are on the field. This becomes extremely noticeable in the higher level areas where enemies have massive health pools and can attack from nearly anywhere on the map. The Medusa enemy being the biggest offender. If there’s more than one in a mission, you'd better be prepare for endless spam while you mostly sit there blocking and slowly getting chipped to death. Later in the game, enemies can attack up to three times per turn. That means two or three enemies can generate anywhere from 6–9 incoming attacks every round. At lower levels this isn’t a huge issue, but later on you spend so much time repositioning and defending that offensive play barely feels viable unless you intentionally leave yourself exposed to attacks. Again, it wouldn't be much of an issue if they didn't deal high damage. My biggest issue, though, is that the overall gameplay loop becomes repetitive and tedious very quickly. It boils down to taking contracts > fighting robots > collect rewards > upgrade > repeat. That gameplay loop works in a series like Monster Hunter because those games have a huge amount of mechanical depth and encounter variety. Here, the combat isn’t engaging enough to want to play hundreds of repetitive battles. The story also isn't interesting enough to carry me to the end. It's a very Saturday morning cartoon or tokusatsu style of story telling. Admittedly, it isn't trying to be very deep, but it has also failed to be even slightly entertaining. The characters are nonexistent, and the custom party system somehow feels even more shallow than XCOM 2 soldiers. I never played the Early Access version, but somehow this still feels exactly like an EA game. In my opinion, it needed a lot more time in the oven. I’ll probably keep playing long enough to try the other mechs, and I hope future updates flesh things out more, but right now I can’t recommend it. Edit: How could I forget to mention the UI? I have only one word for it. Terrible. All the menus are so cumbersome. How did this make it out of early access? The character creation is near unusable and the ship having like 4 screens I need to manually navigate back and forth between just sucks. Like, why was this not worked on more? I have seen discussions about this very thing from a year ago, so it's not like the developers weren't aware.

The game is very fun with a strong core, though I can see why some people are divided on it. The game took me about 20 hours to beat, and I did a good chunk of the sidequests on the way. The art style is nice, and the color palette really pops. The biggest aspect that will determine if you like the game is the battle system. The game is turn based and uses a timeline where you determine what actions are performed and when. There are also four quadrants that units can place themselves in. After you place an action on the timeline, the enemy units then place theirs. You have four crewmates that can each take an individual action, or have them pass their actions to each other if their relationship is developed enough. After all of the actions for a round are determined, then the round plays out. There's a lot to think about when planning the entire turn, and it can get somewhat confusing at times if you don't keep track. There are some lite RPG elements in the game in the form of personal traits and skills. They're mostly minor buffs with the occasional strong skill showing up as you raise each character's proficiency. You also have to manage some resources like fuel, mood and fatigue. Characters can go through mental breakdowns, epiphanies and even die if battles go poorly enough. It's not the deepest system, but it works for the most part. I suppose the weakest aspect of the game is the story, which is just OK. Its not bad, to be clear, and the plot overall makes sense. I really didn't find myself bored going through it, but it lacks compelling characters, since your crew is a bunch of randomly generated characters by default. There is a character customization option that you can use to make your own crew, and it's not too shabby. But don't expect anything deep. The game is worth the price, at least in my opinion. I didn't really have many complaints throughout. I know that might not be the same for everyone, but I had a good time and can recommend it to any one who wants a fresh turn based mecha game to sink their teeth into.

I really like the base concept of having an RPG playing like an anime mech fight, and have the pilots live their own stories and relationships. The art style is really interesting as well. Unfortunately, this is all the praise I can give this game. The fights look cool in the trailer, but when every action always plays the same few seconds of a clip, and you have 3 moves, it gets repetitive really quickly and the novelty wears off. Yeah, you can skip those, but then you lose all the appeal of the anime fight, and are left with a pretty barebones turn based system with 4 characters of which only 2 of them can attack, one just presses a button, and one runs out of ammo for the support move. Pilots are procedurally generated as well, which is cool in the sense that you can reroll them many, many times and see a lot of cool combinations, but this means that their personalities are cookiecutters, and often don't match their designs or expressions. I had a pilot who had an idol pose, smiling to the camera doing the victory sign, and she was the one designated to deliver the most depressing and jarring lines in that pose, which was an absurd experience. [i] I want to love Nitro Gen Omega (NGO), I truly do. The art style and music fit the gameplay perfectly, and the combat is some of the most unique I’ve seen in an indie title. [/i] [h1]📝 Main Pros, Cons, and Suggestions, followed by the Review:[/h1] 🟩 Pros: + Can design all 4 crew members + Plenty of creative ideas that show real ambition + Strong anime art direction that perfectly complements the gameplay + Distinctive combat system that feels genuinely fresh within the mech strategy genre + Ability success depends on heat, and damage taken depends on hull health, both adding risk reward elements 🟥 Cons: - Bugs - UI/UX - World map is empty - The story lacks depth - Half the crew often feel underutilised during fights - Inability to cancel queued actions makes combat feel restrictive - Forced action assignment for every crew member slows battles down unnecessarily - Still feels too much like an early access title at its current price 🏷️ Suggestions: ~ Option to redo prior turn crew action ~ Option to skip remaining crew action ~ Ability to undo crew action selection ~ More overworld activities and contract variability [h1] It’s clunky, lacks polish, and still feels very much like an early access title, especially given then price [/h1] There are three core parts to the game: Completing combat contracts, obtaining mech parts to unlock new crew skills, and managing morale and friendships between your crew. On paper, it all comes together brilliantly. In practice, it quickly boils down to taking contracts, fighting robots, collecting underwhelming rewards, upgrading your mech, and repeating the cycle. The biggest issues come from the moment to moment friction. You can’t end your turn without assigning every crew member an action, even if that action is just skipping their turn. You also can’t cancel actions once they’ve been placed in the battle timeline. It also doesn’t help that half your crew often feel like they contribute very little during combat, which makes the forced action assignment feel even more tedious. [h1] These frustrations start small, but after a couple of hours they became consistently irritating [/h1] Reviews are divided, and fairly so. NGO is clearly trying something different, and I respect the ambition. While the execution isn’t quite there yet, there’s still something genuinely interesting underneath the rough edges. I wish I could give a neutral review. If you can tolerate the clunkiness and push through the lack of polish, there’s a unique mech strategy experience here that may click with you. If you're interested, add it to your wishlist and wait until it's at least 75% off. At that price point, I recommend it - For now, it's best if you sit on the sideline. Updated review after 40 hours of the game Probably the game with best presentation I've played recently, the combat, the art style, the music, everything just ooze with deliberate style, but not too much that it becomes overbearing. It's easy, for example, for a dev to get lost in their own sauce and make the combat unbearably slow or complicated, but the dev of this game understand that a game still have to be playable. Combat is really, really underwhelming early on, but it get a lot more interesting later when both you and your enemies have more things to do. So the meat and bone of the game is really on my wheelhouse. I can't underline enough how much I like the style and the actual combat. But my main complaint is that the user interface is really bad and there's a lot of really grating design decisions. For example: - There's no easy way to check your pilots' stats while assigning them to stations in your mech, which is really weird UI decision. In any games where you can assign units, you would want to know what skill your pilots have when you assign them to something. In this game you have to check a separate page for your characters first. - Related to that, you also can't check recipe on cooking menu if you have the recipe. You have to actually check your inventory and see what the recipe is. And even if you do, the recipe doesn't actually tell you what its effect. Does it give bonus hp? Extra melee defense? You just have to remember them. - Navigating your ship's rooms is really awkward. -Skipping cutscene doesn't actually tell you the result of that cutscene. Say you're crafting something, and you're treated with a crafting cutscene. It's nice, but after a while, you just want to skip the cutscene. Generally games would skip the cutscene and give you to a text screen with something like "Crafting result: Masterwork Bear Armor" or whatever. In this game, there is no such text result. - Gating access to different mechs on really hard quest that you can only beat with late-game mech. By the time you get a different mechs, you'll have a top of the line mech already. And this is compounded by how you only get a basic, weakest version of the other mechs when you unlock them. If you actually want to use them, you'll have to grind money equipment for them all over again. - And talking about finding new equipment, this is probably the most grating design decision for me. Store inventories are semi-randomized (so specific city sell specific mech equipment), but you can't refresh their inventory easily. I still don't know how you can refresh their inventory, but most of the time you'll remember seeing a mech part you want to use when you're low level and have no money, and when you're at high level and you actually have money, you won't be able to find them anymore. It won't be that bad if you can just pray to rng and refresh the store inventories easily, but you can't. Definitely a case of style over substance, but with enough substance that I can actually recommend it if you like the style.
